signals.signal: H1-2026 Romania: net profit EUR 158m (-5.6% y/y; Q2 alone EUR 78m vs EUR 76m), operating revenue EUR 465m (NII EUR 328m, fees EUR 124m), operating costs EUR 166m (-11% y/y), operating profit EUR 247m, cost/income 35.7 cents per EUR 100 of revenue vs 40.0 a year earlier; loans EUR 13.5bn (+EUR 1bn y/y, +8.3%), deposits EUR 14.9bn (from EUR 14.4bn). FTEs 4,261 vs 4,851 in H1-2025 (-12.2%).
signals.source_name: BankingNews.ro, reporting UniCredit S.p.A. 2Q26 country disclosure
signals.implies: 590 fewer FTEs in a year while the loan book grows is the classic signature of a bank moving transactions off the counter. The tools that let a smaller branch workforce keep serving cash customers are teller cash recyclers, assisted self-service pods and outsourced first/second-line ATM service - Printec's cash-automation and managed-services lines.
signals.likelihood: High that the cost/FTE reduction continues through 2026-27
signals.followup: Pull UniCredit Bank SA's own IFRS interim report (BVB filing, bond issuer UCB27/UCB29) for the audited 30/06/2026 branch and ATM counts.

signals.signal: Bank's own 'About us at a glance' page: nationwide network of 253 branches and 4,475 employees at 31/12/2025; FY2025 consolidated profit EUR 296m, loans EUR 13.2bn, deposits EUR 15.1bn. Shareholding at 15/08/2025: UniCredit S.p.A. 89.09%, Alpha International Holdings SMSA 9.9%, Romanian individuals 0.96%, Romanian companies 0.04%.
signals.source_name: UniCredit Bank Romania - 'About us at a glance' (bank's own website)
signals.implies: 253 branches at 31/12/2025 against 'approximately 300' announced at merger completion on 18/08/2025 = roughly 47 units closed in about 4.5 months. Each closure is a decision point: keep an off-site ATM/recycler at the site, or lose the cash footprint. That decision window is where an ATM + cash-automation + managed-services vendor gets in.
signals.followup: Request the closed-branch list; establish whether closed sites retained an off-site ATM and who services it.

signals.signal: Bank told Ziarul Financiar it will keep 'approximately 200 branches' across all counties by end-2026 while denying any 'massive restructuring' for 2026 or later years - down from ~300 at merger completion and 253 at 31/12/2025.
signals.source_name: Business24.ro citing a UniCredit statement given to Ziarul Financiar
signals.implies: A further ~50 closures inside 2026. Networks that shrink this fast usually (a) redeploy or relocate ATMs, (b) add deposit-capable units at the surviving sites to absorb the cash volume, and (c) move a now more dispersed fleet onto a managed-service contract. All three are directly Printec-addressable.
signals.likelihood: High within 6 months - the target is end-2026
signals.followup: Track the branch count monthly on the bank's locator (iframe at https://ro.unicreditbanking.net/branch/map?country=ro); ask who does ATM first-line/second-line service today.

signals.signal: Retail EVP Antoaneta Curteanu: the bank will go from 2 branches with 'Prime corners' today to 40 units with Prime offices within a year, explicitly funded out of the post-Alpha network consolidation - 'network optimisations were made after the merger with Alpha Bank... many branches were very close together so we had to consolidate them. We take the occasion to also refit the spaces and adapt the business model.' New Calea Dorobanti branch (in a former OTP Bank unit) inaugurated 14/07/2026 with 2 Prime offices. Prime clients to go from ~25,000 today to 50,000-60,000 within a year. CEO Mihaela Lupu: 'when everyone wants only digitalisation, our strategy is to keep human contact'.
signals.implies: A dated, funded refit programme covering ~38 more branches in 12 months. A refit is the moment a bank re-specifies in-branch cash and client-facing tech: teller cash recyclers to free the banker from the till, assisted self-service pods, queue/appointment management, and tablet-based digital onboarding at the desk. This is the single most actionable Printec opening at this bank right now.
signals.likelihood: High - stated 12-month plan, first two units already live
signals.followup: Get the refit specification and the incumbent branch fit-out / cash-automation supplier; approach before the 2027 tranche is specified.

signals.signal: Group primary confirmation of the Prime model: launched 13/05/2026 simultaneously across nine CEE markets (Bulgaria, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Croatia, Czechia, Hungary, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia). Package explicitly includes 'exclusive Prime zones in selected branches for privacy and comfort', priority in branches and call centres, and a dedicated in-app section. Based on research with over 11,000 clients; tested in the top 25% of more than 1,000 service concepts.
signals.implies: 'Prime zones in selected branches' is a group-mandated branch-format change replicated across nine CEE countries, not a Romanian one-off. A vendor that wins the Romanian refit specification has a template to pitch into Bulgaria, Serbia, Croatia and B&H - all Printec footprint markets.
signals.likelihood: Rolling out now across nine markets
signals.followup: Ask UniCredit Bulbank (Prime zones already in ALL branches per baseline) what hardware sits in a Prime zone, then reuse the answer in Romania and Serbia.

signals.signal: Romanian Competition Council fined 10 banks RON 3.73bn (EUR 710m) on 07/06/2026 for coordinated conduct in the ROBOR fixing procedure; UniCredit Bank SA's share is RON 431.03m (the third largest after BT RON 960m and BCR RON 577m). UniCredit issued a formal statement rejecting the decision as 'unjust, unfounded' and confirmed it will challenge it in court. Banks have 60 days from receipt of the reasoned decision to submit action plans to eliminate the practices. Investigation opened end-2022.
signals.source_name: Economedia.ro (per-bank amounts) + UniCredit Bank Romania press release of 17/06/2026
signals.implies: Two vendor consequences: (1) a RON 431m contingent liability makes 2026-27 procurement favour opex/lease/as-a-service structures over capex - pitch ATM-as-a-Service and managed services, not box sales; (2) the mandated remediation action plan pushes budget into surveillance, communications monitoring and control tooling, adjacent to Printec's AML/compliance and transaction-monitoring lines.
signals.likelihood: Certain that the decision stands for now; litigation will run years
signals.followup: Retrieve the reasoned decision from consiliulconcurentei.ro when published (site returned 503 this run) and read the remediation obligations verbatim.

signals.signal: On the 2Q26 earnings call UniCredit S.p.A. flagged around EUR 140m of potential extraordinary negative impacts from Banca Progetto and the ROBOR developments in Romania, while raising FY2026 group net-profit guidance to 'significantly above EUR 11bn' (c.EUR 11.5bn excluding integration costs) and the FY2028 target to above EUR 13bn / FY2030 to above EUR 15bn.
signals.source_name: Investing.com transcript of UniCredit 2Q 2026 earnings call
signals.implies: The group has ring-fenced the Romanian legal exposure as a one-off rather than cutting investment. Romanian transformation budgets (branch refit, Prime, cloud) therefore look protected - keep selling, but expect procurement to prefer subscription pricing.
signals.likelihood: Medium - the charge only lands if the fine crystallises
signals.followup: Read the 2Q26 interim report note on provisions for legal risks once published on unicreditgroup.eu.

signals.signal: UniCredit Group 2Q26 results deck sets out the technology agenda: 'strengthen the partnership with IBM and build a new IT infrastructure operating model with Accenture'; 'accelerating transition to cloud... through our partnership with Google Cloud'; and 'deploying targeted AI solutions to accelerate key processes such as KYC, Corporate Lending, and Transaction Monitoring'. Also: founding member of a euro stablecoin with Qivalis, active contributor to the Digital Euro pilot, three tokenisation POCs, 1.1k data-and-AI staff, organisational structures down 45% vs Dec-2020 - with a footnote stating that for Romania this figure 'includes intake, recast and simplification of Alpha Bank'.
signals.source_name: UniCredit S.p.A., 2Q26 Group Results presentation (PDF, pp.5-6)
signals.implies: Direct competitive read-across: the group is buying KYC, transaction monitoring and AML automation centrally on Google Vertex AI with IBM/Accenture as infrastructure partners. Printec should not pitch a competing central AML engine into UniCredit Romania; the winnable ground is the physical/edge layer the group deck does not cover - ATMs, recyclers, in-branch self-service, POS estate, HSM/key management and field managed services.
signals.followup: Confirm whether ATM/branch-device management is in scope of the Accenture IT-infrastructure operating model or stays local.

signals.signal: RE-VERIFIED (baseline item): the 10-year Google Cloud MoU covering 13 UniCredit markets including Romania was signed 12/05/2025; scope is progressive migration of core and legacy applications, Vertex AI and Gemini models, with named use cases including financial-crime prevention, and optional Google Maps Platform use. Confirmed still the stated cloud direction in the 2Q26 deck.
signals.source_name: UniCredit Bank Romania press release (Romanian text of the group announcement)
signals.implies: Confirms the AML/financial-crime and analytics layer is a group-level Google Cloud build. Reinforces the recommendation above: sell the edge and the service wrap, not the central platform.
signals.followup: Establish which Romanian applications have actually migrated and whether card/ATM switching is in scope.

signals.signal: Official tariff schedule CD102 rev.32/03.07.2026 (in force from 03/07/2026) confirms the ATM operating model: free unlimited RON withdrawals at 'the bank's ATMs and Euronet' in Romania; the footnote states plainly that 'Euronet is a payment processor that owns an independent ATM network in Romania, a UniCredit Bank partner'. Cash deposit into the customer's account by physical debit card at 'Multifunctionalele de numerar (BNA)' is a standard included operation, as are ATM/BNA balance enquiry and barcode-based garnishment withdrawals. Fifth and subsequent other-bank withdrawals in a month cost 1.5%, minimum RON 5.
signals.source_name: UniCredit Bank Romania, 'Comisioane si dobanzi - Persoane Fizice' PDF (CD102 rev.32)
signals.implies: Two things matter. (1) Euronet is the entrenched off-site extension of UniCredit's fleet, so a pure off-site ATM proposal will be measured against an existing free-of-charge third-party network - this is the same Euronet dynamic Printec already faces at Raiffeisen RO and CrediaBank GR. (2) The bank's own estate is explicitly deposit-capable (BNA multifunctional units) and cash-in is free to the customer, which means deposit volume - and therefore recycler demand - sits on the bank's own machines as branches close.
signals.followup: Establish the split of the c.900-unit fleet between cash-out ATMs and deposit-capable BNAs, and the OEM - still unidentified. Ask whether the Euronet arrangement is acceptance-only or extends to operating the bank's own machines.

signals.signal: UniCredit Bank went live with RoPay - Romania's national instant-payment overlay (pay by phone number or QR code, settled in under 10 seconds, 24/7/365) - inside both Mobile Banking and Business Mobile, including alias management and in-person QR payment. Implementation partner was Montran, supplier of the central RoPay and Instant Payments platforms. TRANSFOND stated c.8.8 million users could then transact by phone alias. RoPay is built by TRANSFOND with the Romanian Banking Association under BNR authorisation.
signals.source_name: UniCredit Bank Romania press release (AEM press-release endpoint)
signals.implies: Consumer- and merchant-presented QR is now live at a bank with a large Micro/SME book. That shifts acceptance economics away from card rails and creates demand for QR-capable terminals, softPOS on merchant phones, and merchant reconciliation - Printec's POS/acquiring line. It also names Montran, not the incumbent card processor, as the payments-rails integrator in Romania.
signals.followup: Check whether RoPay QR is being pushed onto the bank's physical POS estate and who supplies and services those terminals.

signals.signal: UniCredit Bank extended its ShopSmart card-linked offers programme from retail (over 500,000 enrolled individual clients) into the Business Mobile app for the Micro segment on 13/07/2026; benefits apply to card payments at partner merchants across all eligible company cards.
signals.implies: A card-linked-offer engine now spanning consumer and Micro segments means the bank is investing in merchant-side data and acquiring relationships. That is the natural door-opener for POS/acquiring and merchant-services conversations.
signals.followup: Identify the ShopSmart offer-engine vendor and whether the bank acquires the partner merchants itself.

signals.signal: UniCredit Bank launched an in-app and website chat channel for retail clients on 06/07/2026, explicitly positioned as 'an efficient alternative to call-centre phone calls', covering app configuration, cards, transactions and products, with hand-off to a human consultant for complex cases. Romanian language only at launch.
signals.implies: Channel-cost deflection is running in parallel with the FTE cut. A bank deflecting service interactions is also a bank that will accept assisted self-service in branch - the same logic applied to the cash counter.
signals.followup: Find out whether the chat is AI-backed (Gemini/Vertex under the Google Cloud deal) or rule-based with agent hand-off.

signals.signal: Alpha Bank Romania IT integration detail: TotalSoft harmonised the two banks' ERP and HR platforms onto Charisma ERP and Charisma HCM over roughly 6 months, covering c.4,800 staff, plus contract management, procurement, internal expense management, GDPR applications, eFactura e-invoicing and new financial reporting - explicitly to keep the merged ~300 branches and 900 ATMs running without interruption.
signals.implies: Confirms the back-office side of the merger is done and names a local integrator (TotalSoft) already inside the bank. The ATM/self-service estate is conspicuously the one layer with no publicly named vendor - which is exactly where a harmonisation decision is still open after absorbing Alpha's machines.
signals.followup: STANDING TASK: identify the ATM OEM and the field-service provider for the combined ~900-unit fleet. Not disclosed anywhere public this run.

signals.signal: CEO Mihaela Lupu at ZF Bankers Summit: the bank is 'in the consolidation period' after closing the Alpha merger, aims to 'grow above the market' in 2026 as it did in the merger year, and will 'continue to invest in technology and in client experience, especially retail'; positions the bank third in lending; names resilience/stability, digitalisation-and-client-expectations, and people/skills as the three priorities; says AI cannot replace fundamentals.
signals.implies: Retail technology and client experience are the stated 2026 spend priority from the CEO. That is the budget line a branch cash-automation and self-service proposal would be funded from.
signals.followup: Get the 2026 IT/technology budget figure - UniCredit RO does not publish one the way BT and CEC do.

signals.signal: Market context (BNR H2-2025 payment statistics, published 17/05/2026): Romania had 11,136 ATMs from resident payment service providers at 31/12/2025, up 1,108 in six months; 729,408 POS terminals (+161,396); 685,731 EFTPOS points (+120,300); 28.63m active cards (+10.07% vs June 2025), of which 24.68m with a cash function.
signals.source_name: Agerpres, reporting Banca Nationala a Romaniei payment statistics
signals.implies: The Romanian ATM base grew c.11% in one half-year while branches shrank - the market is substituting machines for counters at pace, and POS grew 28% in six months. Both are volume tailwinds for an ATM/POS vendor, and they make UniCredit's c.900-unit fleet roughly 8% of the national estate.
signals.followup: Pull the BNR primary series directly (www.bnr.ro/Indicatori-plati-5291.aspx redirected/302 to the fetch tool this run) to split on-us vs third-party ATM deployers.

signals.signal: UniCredit Bank raised RON 600m in a bond issue announced 02/03/2026, adding to the outstanding UCB27 and UCB29 issues on which coupon notices were published in 2025.
signals.source_name: UniCredit Bank Romania press release archive
signals.implies: Funding is in place; the ROBOR provision is not starving the investment programme. Supports pitching a multi-year refit/fleet programme rather than a single-year purchase.
signals.followup: Confirm size, tenor and use of proceeds from the BVB prospectus.

signals.signal: Digital onboarding baseline (re-verified, not new): UniCredit Bank runs a 100% online current-account opening flow inside Mobile Banking, average under 10 minutes, fully automated, using video selfie, OCR capture of the ID card and AI-based authentication, issuing a virtual Mastercard immediately.
signals.implies: eKYC is already solved and in production, so a greenfield digital-onboarding pitch is closed. The open adjacency is in-branch assisted onboarding for the Prime refit (tablet/desk capture) and identity re-verification at self-service devices.
signals.followup: Identify the eKYC vendor behind the video-selfie/OCR flow.

coverage_notes: Fresh run - no checkpoint existed for 2026-07-30. Angles used: (1) the bank's own AEM press-release archive, enumerated end-to-end via the POST endpoint https://www.unicredit.ro/show.pws.pressrelease.html (all 18 pages, Jan-2025 to Jul-2026) plus keyword queries for bancomate / Google Cloud / RoPay / ShopSmart / Consiliul Concurentei; (2) the bank's own 'at a glance' and tariff PDFs (CD102 rev.32 in force 03/07/2026) parsed locally with pdfminer; (3) UniCredit S.p.A. 2Q26 group results PDF and press release, parsed locally; (4) Romanian-language press (Economedia, HotNews, Business24, Ziarul Financiar, Wall-Street, BankingNews, Agerpres) for the Dorobanti/Prime launch event, the branch-count target and the ROBOR fines; (5) BNR/Agerpres market statistics for the national ATM/POS base. GENUINE GAPS: (a) the ATM fleet OEM and the field-service provider for the combined ~900 units remain unidentified - no public source names them, and the bank's locator (iframe at ro.unicreditbanking.net/branch/map) exposes no queryable API, so I could not even recount the fleet; (b) no published post-merger ATM count later than the 900 stated at merger completion on 18/08/2025; (c) no split between cash-out ATMs and deposit-capable BNA multifunctional units; (d) no published Romanian IT/technology capex figure (unlike BT and CEC, UniCredit RO does not disclose one); (e) UniCredit Bank SA's standalone IFRS interim report for H1-2026 was not found on the bank's site this run, so the H1 figures rest on press reporting of the group disclosure rather than on the bank's own filing.
access_issues: www.unicredit.ro returns HTTP 403 to the plain fetch tool - defeated with a desktop Chrome User-Agent via curl, and for the press archive additionally 'Referer: https://www.unicredit.ro/ro/institutional/centru-media/comunicate-de-presa.html' + 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' against the AEM endpoint /show.pws.pressrelease.html (POST params: _charset_, number, keywords, datefrom, dateto, lang=ro, appName=cee2020-pws-ro). economedia.ro and wall-street.ro also 403 the fetch tool; economedia was retrieved with a desktop-UA curl, wall-street.ro 403'd curl too and was read via the fetch tool instead. www.consiliulconcurentei.ro/comunicate-de-presa/ returned HTTP 503 (logged - the primary ROBOR decision text could not be opened, so per-bank fine amounts come from Economedia). www.bnr.ro/Indicatori-plati-5291.aspx returned HTTP 302 to the fetch tool and to desktop-UA curl, so BNR payment statistics come from Agerpres. https://www.unicredit.ro/ro/institutional/localizare-sucursale-atm.html 302s to error404; the working page is /ro/institutional/sucursale-atm.html but its branch/ATM data lives in a third-party iframe (ro.unicreditbanking.net/branch/map) whose data endpoint I could not locate (probed /branch/search, /branch/branches, /branch/locations, /branch/rest/branch, /api/branches - all 404/403). No source was dropped silently.
operator_requests: 1) UniCredit Bank S.A. standalone H1-2026 IFRS interim report (issuer of UCB27/UCB29 bonds) - should be filed with BVB and would give the audited 30/06/2026 branch and ATM counts; not located on unicredit.ro this run. 2) The Romanian Competition Council's reasoned ROBOR decision (site 503) - needed to read UniCredit's RON 431.03m share and the mandated remediation obligations verbatim. 3) BNR's primary 'Indicatori plati' series (302 to automated fetch) for the ATM/POS breakdown by deployer.
